A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniSplat and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across the restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on six datasets, an optimization-iteration ablation, and segmentation/editing demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds encoder/rasterizer ablations and quantitative segmentation-matching results.

M1.justification: The core Yin-Yang decomposition, MVSplat-based estimation, rendering, and optional optimization remain. v2 explicitly describes alpha-normalized rendering and single-best attention matching, whereas v1 gives a general rasterizer description and top-K voting/merging details. The PDFs do not establish whether these differences reflect implementation changes or changes in documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover OmniBlender, Ricoh360, OmniPhotos, 360Roam, OmniScenes, and 360VO, with synthesis and segmentation/editing already present in v1. Appendix Tables B–G retain the same 61 scenes and reference/test-view indices.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PanoGRF, DepthSplat (O), and MVSplat (Y) across all six datasets, substantially broadening the comparisons. Appendix Tables B–G add the latter two. Existing reconstruction comparators and DEVA remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled encoder/rasterizer replacement experiments and an mIoU evaluation using full-sequence DEVA tracking as pseudo ground truth. Existing reconstruction splits, image resolution, metrics, and optimization budgets remain unchanged; the newly stated depth bounds are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's optimization-iteration ablation, v2 directly tests Yin-Yang encoding and rasterization separately on OmniPhotos and OmniScenes in Table 2. The MVSplat (Y) comparison also tests naive Yin-Yang input adaptation, providing substantial new analysis of the central design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises OmniSplat and OmniSplat+opt scores across all six datasets; for example, OmniBlender OmniSplat PSNR changes from 21.02 to 21.22 and LPIPS from 0.3231 to 0.3636. New baseline, component-ablation, and segmentation results are added. Table A's best LPIPS shifts from 200 to 400 iterations. However, Tables B–G retain the earlier OmniSplat values, leaving the revised main results inconsistent with the appendix.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the warping formula's source feature and mask indices and changes mask normalization from M^n to M^i: compare v1 Eqs. (3)–(4) with v2 Eqs. (4)–(5). These correct mathematical expressions; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 removes segmentation/editing from the abstract and replaces the corresponding contribution bullet with explicit transfer without fine-tuning. Reconstruction and efficiency remain the central claims, while segmentation/editing survives as a secondary application.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of naive MVSplat (Y) feature averaging, alpha-related brightness artifacts, and the separate effects of encoding and rasterization. The limitations concerning interpolation quality and adaptation efficiency are substantially retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies depth bounds of 1 and 100, details alpha normalization and camera rotation during rendering, and supplies a project-page URL. Conversely, it omits v1's detailed segment-voting and directional-graph merging description. These are documentation changes without verified changes in implementation or online resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands sparse-view reconstruction positioning through works such as LoopSparseGS, DNGaussian, CoherentGS, DepthSplat, GRM, and GS-LRM. It removes the dedicated 3D-editing related-work subsection and GaussianEditor/TIP-Editor references, shifting the literature emphasis toward reconstruction.

P1.justification: The method overview and contribution list are substantially rewritten. Rasterization becomes a standalone Section 3.2, while segmentation documentation is shortened and redistributed into Section 4.2 and Appendix B. Related work and supplementary sections are reorganized, alongside widespread language editing.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is extensively redrawn, Figure 1 changes its benchmark and display, Tables 2–3 are added, and comparison tables gain rows or columns. Segmentation examples are split between the main text and appendix, the removal example is relocated, and supplementary qualitative grids are reorganized with additional comparator panels.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, direct component ablations, quantitative segmentation evaluation, and corrected equations strengthen the paper. However, v2 introduces wider numerical inconsistencies: v1's Table 1 and Table B agree on OmniBlender OmniSplat PSNR 21.02, whereas v2 reports 21.22 in Table 1 but retains 21.02 in Table B. Similar conflicts affect the other datasets without an explained setting difference. The stronger validation and reduced numerical coherence leave the net quality change uncertain.
